Yes, I read the changelog. The only relevant line in the 2.5.0 section is "Refactor LineList and spectral frame handling (#812)". Nobody can tell from that that a default changed. I found the cause today by reading the diff, and it is not my calibration or my config.

PR #812 (merged Oct 22) changes the default in LineList.__init__ from wave_frame='air' to wave_frame='vacuum'. Rest wavelengths are now vacuum unless you say otherwise. My spectra are calibrated in air, so every line is compared against the wrong rest wavelength. The vacuum/air ratio at 6563 A is about 1.00028, which is exactly the offset I reported (z lower by 0.00028, about 83 km/s, same direction for every object). There is no deprecation warning.

Workaround for anyone with air-calibrated data:

LineList(..., wave_frame='air')

Or pin lumenfit==2.4.3 until this is sorted out.

"Works for me" does not test this. If your data are already in vacuum, or radio, you would see no difference at all, so identical fits are expected and say nothing about my setup. m_okonkwo also sees an offset in this thread, so it is not only me.

This cost me two days of doubting my wavelength solution, and I re-reduced the arc lamps for 40 spectra for nothing. A pointer to the PR would have helped a lot more than being told to do basic checks and having the thread marked as solved.

@lumenfit_maint, could you please reopen this thread? I'd also ask for one of these, ideally both:

- an explicit line in CHANGES.md for 2.5.0 saying the default wave_frame changed from air to vacuum
- a warning when wave_frame is not set explicitly

Either one would save other people from the same problem.
